title: Prokaryotic cells and viruses; Water
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE04a#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE04a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE04a#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE04a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM01a#N.4a, CE04a#N.3a, BM01a#N.5b, CE04a#N.13a, BM01a#N.9b, BM01a#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Lysozyme
items.clue: An enzyme that strips away the wall of a bacterium

items.label: Prokaryotic
items.clue: Describes cells with no nucleus, such as bacteria and archaea

items.label: Nucleoid
items.clue: Region of cytoplasm where a bacterium's circular DNA lies free

items.label: Peptidoglycan
items.clue: The material of the wall outside a bacterium's plasma membrane

questions.stem: Why is each covalent bond between oxygen and hydrogen in a water molecule polar?

options.text: The shared electrons are drawn more strongly towards the oxygen atom.
Each hydrogen atom gives up its electron completely to the oxygen atom.
It is a hydrogen bond, and hydrogen bonds are polar by their nature.
Oxygen and hydrogen atoms behave as opposite magnetic poles.

questions.explanation: Oxygen attracts the shared electron pair more strongly than hydrogen does, so the electrons are shared unequally: oxygen becomes δ− and each hydrogen δ+.

questions.stem: Which description of the structure of a Bacillus cell is correct?

options.text: A loop of naked DNA lies in the cytoplasm, and proteins are made on 70S ribosomes.
The DNA is enclosed by a nuclear membrane inside a small nucleus within the cytoplasm.
The cell wall outside the plasma membrane is built from long parallel fibres of cellulose.
The DNA loop is wound around histone proteins to package it within the nucleoid region.

questions.explanation: A Gram-positive eubacterium such as Bacillus has a cell wall, a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, naked DNA in a loop lying in the nucleoid region of the cytoplasm, and 70S ribosomes on which its proteins are synthesised.

questions.stem: The model shows three water molecules. The symbols δ+ and δ− show partial charges. Which statement correctly describes the interaction labelled 2 in the model?

options.text: An attraction between the partially positive H of one molecule and the partially negative O of another
A covalent bond in which the H atom of one molecule shares a pair of electrons with the O atom of another
An ionic bond between an H⁺ ion in one molecule and an O²⁻ ion in a second, neighbouring molecule
A strong bond, stronger than line 1, that holds the two water molecules in a fixed position

questions.stem: An electron micrograph shows a cell about 3 µm long. It has a cell wall, a paler fibrous region of DNA not enclosed by any membrane, many small dense granules, and no membrane-bound organelles. How should the cell be classified?

options.text: As a plant cell, because a cell wall is found only around the cells of plants.
As a eukaryote, because the region containing DNA must be a nucleus, as every cell has one.
As a prokaryote, because its DNA lies in a nucleoid region and it has no membrane-bound organelles.
As a eukaryote, because prokaryotic cells are too simple to contain any ribosomes.

questions.stem: Glucose is carried dissolved in blood plasma and in phloem sap, and it is broken down by enzymes in the aqueous cytoplasm. Which property of glucose makes this possible?

options.text: It separates into positive and negative ions in water.
It is a small molecule, and small molecules dissolve readily.
Its many hydroxyl (–OH) groups form hydrogen bonds with water.
Water breaks its covalent bonds, splitting it into soluble fragments.

questions.explanation: The polar –OH groups of glucose hydrogen-bond with water, so glucose is hydrophilic and dissolves. It can then be transported in plasma and phloem sap and acted on by enzymes in solution.

questions.stem: In blood plasma, glucose travels freely dissolved. Cholesterol does not: it travels inside lipoprotein particles whose outer surface carries polar and charged groups. Why does cholesterol need this carrier?

options.text: Cholesterol molecules are too large to fit between water molecules and dissolve.
Water molecules push cholesterol away with a repulsive force between them.
Cholesterol is largely non-polar, so it forms few attractions with water.
Glucose splits into ions in water, but cholesterol stays as whole molecules.

questions.explanation: With almost no δ+ or δ− regions, cholesterol cannot hydrogen-bond with water; it is hydrophobic. The carrier's polar, charged surface is attracted to water and carries the cholesterol through the plasma.
